VOICE: Respond in clear, plain, professional English — concise and precise, no affectation.
TAGLINE: A portable, theme-able harness you implant into any repository to grow a disciplined AI agent.
LOADED_SIGIL: ✅ Harness loaded — rules in force, agents and skills ready.
EPI_ONTOLOGY: What this agent is for, and how it decides — read before any rule below.
EPI_LAWS: The rules below hold in every task, in every repository.
EPI_DOCTRINES: Optional rule sets. Only the ones this repository enabled appear here.
EPI_AGENTS: Send the right specialist instead of doing everything in one context.
EPI_SKILLS: Run the written procedure before improvising.
EPI_MEMORY: What is worth keeping must outlive the session in writing.
EPI_VAULT: Read where you were installed — it holds more than the harness.
EPI_CONTEXT: Point the agent at the project's own docs, wherever they live.
EPI_SCRIPTS: Optional automation for teams that want hard enforcement.
BENEDICTION: Work with discipline, keep the rules, and ship clean.
DESC_REVIEWER: Reviews a change for correctness and quality before it merges.
DESC_DEVELOPER: Implements the scoped change in an isolated worktree, self-checked and ready for the tester.
DESC_ARCHITECT: Produces a design or implementation plan before code is written.
DESC_DOCS: Writes and updates user-facing documentation after code lands.
DESC_SECURITY: Audits changes that touch the security surface.
DESC_EXPLORER: Reads and searches widely in a throwaway context, returns only distilled findings.
DESC_RESEARCHER: Searches and fetches the open web in a throwaway context, cross-checks every claim against two sources, returns only sourced findings.
DESC_ADVOCATE: Argues the strongest case for the proposal — the upside, the opportunity, the cost of not acting.
DESC_SKEPTIC: Plays devil's advocate — attacks the proposal for failure modes, risks, and hidden assumptions.
DESC_PRAGMATIST: Weighs feasibility — the cost, effort, and complexity against whether the payoff is worth it.
DESC_STEWARD: Defends the long term — architecture, maintainability, debt, and fit with the system's direction.
DESC_VISIONARY: Argues the bold, transformative version — the 10x upside and what it would take to aim there.
DESC_USER_ADVOCATE: Speaks for whoever uses the outcome — their experience, their friction, what they'd actually ask for.
DESC_FRAMER: Questions the problem itself — whether the motion solves the real need or just a symptom.
DESC_EMPIRICIST: Demands evidence — holds every claim, for and against, to data, tests, or precedent.
DESC_OPERATOR: Speaks for running it in production — reliability, observability, rollback, and the on-call burden.
DESC_HISTORIAN: Brings the precedent — what was tried before, how it went, and the lesson for this decision.
DESC_PLAN: Write a plan to a file before executing a non-trivial task; track progress as you go.
DESC_DEPENDENCIES: Audit the dependencies — outdated, vulnerable, abandoned, unused — into a risk-ordered plan, then upgrade one change at a time with the tests green between.
DESC_GIT_HISTORY: Learn from the git history read-only — bisect, blame, pickaxe — or recover and rewrite it safely — reflog, undo, rebase behind a backup branch.
DESC_DOCUMENT_PROJECT: Write the project's PRD, design system, architecture and AGENTS.md from the code, reconcile the doc tree, and regenerate the offline HTML overview.
DESC_COMMIT: Stage the right paths and write a focused commit.
DESC_CODE_REVIEW: Review a diff or PR for correctness first, quality second.
DESC_BRAINSTORM: Turn a raw idea into an approved design before any code is written.
DESC_CODEBASE_DESIGN: Design deep modules and the domain language around them — small interfaces at deliberate seams, a living GLOSSARY.md, an ADR for each hard-to-reverse decision.
DESC_WAYFINDER: Chart work too big for one session as a shared map of decision tickets, resolved one at a time until the way is clear.
DESC_PROTOTYPE: Answer a design question with throwaway code — built to learn, never to keep.
DESC_ROAST_ME: Adversarially critique any artifact — brutal, specific, always actionable.
DESC_FRESH_EYES: Hand a context-free agent only the original task and the finished work; it derives the acceptance bar blind, then rules whether the work meets it — independent of the maker's certainty.
ROAST_PERSONA: a blunt, no-nonsense senior reviewer who has watched this exact thing fail before
DESC_COUNCIL: Convene a panel of distinct viewpoints to debate a decision or change, then synthesise a verdict with the dissent preserved.
DESC_DEBUG: Find and fix a bug by evidence — a command that fails on it, isolate, root-cause, verify — a red CI run included, reproduced under CI's own conditions.
DESC_REFACTOR: Improve code structure without changing behaviour — one named move, tests green throughout.
DESC_PONYTAIL: Force the laziest solution that works — minimal and shortest-path; stdlib and native before custom code, one line before fifty. lite/full/ultra.
DESC_PARALLEL_AGENTS: Fan independent subtasks out to concurrent subagents, then converge the results.
DESC_PIPELINE: Spawn a small crew — analyst, developer, tester — to work a substantial task in its own worktree, merging only once the tests and lint pass.
DESC_LOOP: Work a requirement in small, scored iterations on a loop/* branch, stepping the geneseed loop engine.
DESC_BRICK_FORGE: Author or adapt a loop brick, then check it with geneseed loop check.
DESC_DEVELOP: Drive a change through the cover-and-verify loop — smallest change, tests written for it, the affected suite green, committed slice by slice.
DESC_TEACH: Teach the user toward a result — a crash course from zero to functional, confusing material decoded until it clicks, or a day-by-day path to a deadline.
DESC_QUIZ: Test what the user knows instead of explaining it — a drill to reflex, an explain-it-back check, or a mastery claim stress-tested — with a blunt readout of the gaps.
DESC_LEARN_MODE: Learn while building — the user designs at each checkpoint, the agent writes only the agreed code and explains it, and the mode persists per project across sessions.
DESC_SECURITY_AUDIT: Review a change for how it would be attacked and what it leaks — trust boundaries, the classic vulnerability classes, secrets, the supply chain — ending in a ship / fix / block verdict.
DESC_SKILL_FORGE: Author, sharpen, merge, or retire a skill — reuse first, trigger before procedure, tested against its neighbours, every satellite registered, doctor green.
DESC_WORKTREE: Isolate a task in its own git worktree from a clean base — look before branching, work only there, integrate through the normal gate, remove it when merged.
DESC_HANDOFF: Snapshot task state so a fresh context — or another agent — can resume in one read.
DESC_SHIP: Open a pull request with a structured body, or finish and merge a branch, once the change is verified.
DESC_RELEASE: Cut a release — bump the version, update the changelog, and tag — keeping all three in sync.
DESC_INGEST: Convert a PDF, Office, or web document into clean markdown before reading it.
DESC_RESEARCH: Answer a question from the open web — search widely, then verify each claim against independent sources before citing it.
DESC_HERDR: Drive herdr from inside it — split panes, spawn sibling agents, wait on output, read other panes.
DESC_RULE: Ask first whether the user wants a standing rule or a durable memory, then write the memory or pressure-test the rule before adopting it in user-rules.md — and tend the memory set: merge, retire, promote.
DESC_PROFILE: Interview the user and draft or refresh PROFILE.md — who they are, how they work, how they like answers pitched; identity only, standing rules route to user-rules.md.
DESC_GENESEED: Operate the deployed Geneseed harness — find each install and its settings, read its files, run status, doctor and diff, and rebuild it with one setting changed when the user asks — and make the user's own OpenCode colour theme.
DESC_REVIEW_RESPONSE: Respond to review feedback with rigour — verify each point, then apply it or decline it with reasons.
DOC_EDIT_THE_SOURCE_NOT_THE_SURFACE: Edit the Source, Not the Surface
DOC_RECORD_THE_PROBE_NOT_THE_SNAPSHOT: Record the Probe, Not the Snapshot
INTRO_DOC: This file is the entry point an AI coding agent reads when working in this repository.
INTRO_AGENTS: Delegate focused work to a specialist rather than doing everything in one context. Each specialist has a single clear purpose and a defined output contract.
INTRO_SKILLS: A Skill is a written procedure for a recurring task. Run the matching Skill before improvising.
INTRO_WORKSPACE: The directory this harness is installed into is its **Workspace**, and it is shared.
INTRO_SCRIPTS: Everything above works on agent self-discipline alone.
EPI_NOTEBOOK: A space of your own — arrange it however serves the work.
INTRO_NOTEBOOK: This is a working space that is **yours alone** — unlike the shared Workspace around you, you own every file here, to create, organise, move, and keep however serves the work. The rules of this space are yours to write — and rewrite — as your practice evolves; code, data, and tools belong here as much as notes.
EPI_WIKI: The user's own knowledge base — consult it first, grow it as you learn.
INTRO_WIKI: The user may keep a personal knowledge base on this machine — an Obsidian vault, or any folder of interlinked markdown notes — that outlives any single repository.
DESC_WIKI: Consult and grow the user's personal knowledge base — find the governing note before acting, write well-linked notes back, file them where they belong.
DESC_MCP: Build or harden a Model Context Protocol server — research the spec, design task-shaped tools, test with the Inspector, and prove it with evaluations.
DESC_BRUNO: Build, reorganise or test a Bruno API collection — requests, environments, assertions, chaining — with every secret a placeholder.
DESC_PROSE: Write prose for a human that doesn't read like a model — cut filler, use active voice, vary rhythm, and trust the reader.
DESC_FRONTEND_DESIGN: Design a UI with a point of view — choose palette, type, and layout for this brief, not the templated defaults, then critique and cut to one bold move.
DESC_WORKFLOW: Run a saved, code-driven workflow that orchestrates subagents deterministically — parallel fan-out, staged pipelines, and verification in a single pass.
